headline: XXIX METAL COMMENCES FIRST LARGE-SCALE DRILL AT THIERRY K1 IN 40 YEARS — 20,000m Bulk-Tonnage Copper-PGE Program Targets Ontario's Largest Primary Copper Resource (TSXV: XXIX)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / XXIX Metal Corp.
snippet: XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV: XXIX) announced on July 20, 2026 that drilling has commenced at the Thierry K1 deposit in northwestern Ontario — the province's largest primary copper resource — marking the first large-scale systematic drill program at Thierry in approximately 40 years. The fully funded 20,000-metre program ($19M+ in treasury) is designed as a bulk-tonnage resource expansion campaign targeting the copper-palladium-platinum system defined by historical work that established Thierry as a high-tonnage, lower-grade primary copper deposit with associated PGE credits. The deposit's scale, Ontario jurisdiction, and PGE by-product credits are the three distinguishing characteristics that separate Thierry K1 from most bulk-tonnage copper targets currently being advanced in Canada. For junior copper-PGE investors, the commencement of drilling after four decades of inactivity — at current copper prices above $4.50/lb and palladium/platinum recovering — is the most concrete signal yet that the economics of bulk-tonnage copper-PGE systems in stable jurisdictions are crossing the threshold of institutional interest.

headline: EQUINOX + ORLA PROXY DEADLINE TODAY — ISS AND GLASS LEWIS BOTH RECOMMEND FOR; SHAREHOLDER VOTE JULY 22 TO CREATE 1M OZ/YEAR NORTH AMERICAN PRODUCER
snippet: The proxy voting deadline for the Equinox Gold (TSX: EQX) and Orla Mining (TSX: OLA) business combination falls today, July 20, 2026 at 9:00 AM Pacific time — with the formal shareholder vote scheduled for July 22 — after both ISS and Glass Lewis recommended shareholders vote FOR the share issuance resolution. Under the terms, each Orla share exchanges for 1.00 Equinox share, with former Orla shareholders holding approximately 33% of the combined company. The combination would create a multi-mine North American gold producer targeting over one million ounces of annual production, consolidating Equinox's operating mines in Canada, Mexico, and Brazil with Orla's Camino Rojo heap leach operation in Zacatecas. Both proxy advisory firm endorsements — ISS and Glass Lewis together represent the majority of institutional proxy voting influence — make the July 22 approval almost certain. For investors tracking mid-tier gold consolidation, the Equinox-Orla combination is the largest North American gold M&A transaction closing this month and creates a company with genuine scale in a sector where sub-500,000-ounce producers increasingly struggle to attract institutional capital.

headline: IEA: COPPER SUPPLY OUTLOOK 'WORSENED CONSIDERABLY' — Sulphuric Acid Crisis From Hormuz Closure Threatens SxEW Producers With 30–60 Day Inventories
snippet: The IEA's updated copper supply assessment — released mid-July 2026 and covered by Mining.com and The Northern Miner — identifies a sulphuric acid supply crisis emerging from the Strait of Hormuz closure and China export restrictions as a compounding threat to SX-EW (solvent extraction-electrowinning) copper producers globally. SX-EW operations, which produce approximately 20% of global refined copper output from oxide ores, depend on continuous sulphuric acid supply; the IEA estimates current inventory cover at 30–60 days for affected producers, with production curtailments possible if the supply disruption extends beyond August. The report explicitly frames copper's supply outlook as having 'worsened considerably' relative to its January 2026 assessment — a direct institutional endorsement of the structural deficit thesis that underpins copper's price support above $4.50/lb. For investors, the acid crisis is an underappreciated secondary risk: it affects operations that were otherwise unimpacted by the Chilean weather events and grade-related issues at Antofagasta covered in prior batches, meaning the aggregate supply impact in H2 2026 may substantially exceed what any single disruption would imply.

headline: VIZSLA COPPER DRILLS 472.8m OF 0.40% CuEq AT THIRA — Phase 2 Two-Rig Program Commencing Late July; 800×900m Open-Pit-Scale Porphyry Footprint Open All Directions (TSXV: VCU)
snippet: Vizsla Copper Corp. (TSXV: VCU) released Phase 1 results from the Thira copper-gold porphyry discovery in central British Columbia on July 16, 2026, reporting hole THI-001 intersecting 472.8 metres of 0.40% copper equivalent from near-surface, including a higher-grade core of 304.8 m averaging 0.48% CuEq — the kind of broad, continuous porphyry intercept that establishes deposit-scale potential before resource definition drilling begins. The current defined mineralized footprint measures approximately 800 × 900 metres and remains open in all directions, with the Phase 1 hole designed to establish vertical extent rather than define limits. Phase 2, a two-rig 8,000-metre program, commences in late July targeting lateral expansion across the entire footprint. For investors tracking BC porphyry copper discoveries, Thira's combination of near-surface depth, broad mineralized intervals, open footprint geometry, and a Phase 2 program already mobilised positions it as one of the most active new copper porphyry programs in British Columbia in the current cycle — a province where recent royalty regime clarity has improved the investment case for pre-resource copper development.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS DRILLS 155.4m AT 1.63 g/t AuEq AT TOMBSTONE — Zone Depth Doubled; Footprint Expands 300m West and South; Maiden Resource Q3 2026 (TSXV: AZT)
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT) announced on July 16, 2026 that drilling at the Tombstone Gold-Silver Project in Arizona has more than doubled the known zone depth while expanding the mineralized footprint 300 metres to the west and south — with hole TBR-001 returning 155.4 metres averaging 1.08 g/t Au and 30.23 g/t Ag (1.63 g/t AuEq) within a broader 198.1-metre intercept. The 87-hole, 17,927-metre reverse circulation program is complete, and a maiden mineral resource estimate is on track for Q3 2026. For investors evaluating gold-silver exploration-stage companies, Tombstone's combination of confirmed zone expansion, doubled depth extent, and an imminent maiden resource estimate is the three-part catalyst schedule that typically drives exploration-stage re-ratings: drill results establish grade continuity (done), footprint expansion establishes resource scale (done), resource estimate converts the drill data into a quantified asset (Q3 2026). Arizona's permitting environment and the project's road-accessible, low-elevation setting add execution predictability to what is otherwise a discovery-stage value proposition.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH CONSECUTIVE SUPPLY DEFICIT: 46.3 MOZ SHORTFALL, 52% BELOW JANUARY ATH — JPM BASE CASE $81, LBMA CONSENSUS $79.57 FOR 2026
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 silver market outlook documents the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit — projected at 46.3 million ounces for 2026 — while silver trades approximately 52% below its January 2026 all-time high of $121.62/oz despite being in structural undersupply. Industrial demand now represents 58% of total silver consumption, with solar panel manufacturing, AI data centre cooling systems, and EV power electronics as the three growth vectors that have structurally separated silver's industrial demand profile from its monetary/investment demand. Two near-term catalysts dominate the outlook: the July 29 FOMC decision (a dovish hold removes the rate-hike headwind that has suppressed silver's monetary premium since February) and Q3 2026 industrial procurement cycles (solar and EV manufacturers typically secure H2 materials in July–August). Institutional consensus: LBMA median forecast $79.57/oz for 2026, J.P. Morgan base case $81/oz. For silver equity investors, the 52% discount to the January ATH combined with the sixth consecutive structural supply deficit is the core asymmetry argument — silver's current price does not reflect its industrial demand trajectory or its supply fundamentals.

headline: WGC BASE CASE: GOLD $4,100 ±5% POST-FOMC JULY 29 — Bull Scenario $4,900–$5,200 if Hormuz Reopens; Central Banks Bought 244 Tonnes in Q1 2026 Alone
snippet: An Allegiance Gold analysis of the July 29 FOMC decision scenarios — drawing on WGC modelling and institutional forecasts — outlines three outcomes for gold: base case (dovish hold, no July hike) targets $4,100 ±5% with one hike still expected by October; bull case (Hormuz reopens, September hike probability collapses) targets $4,900–$5,200 by Q4; bear case (surprise July hike or explicit September signal) compresses toward $3,800–$4,200 with the $4,000 institutional support floor tested. The central bank demand context is critical framing for all three scenarios: central banks globally bought 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 alone — a pace that exceeds full-year 2023 purchases — establishing a structural floor bid that has prevented gold from re-testing $3,800 despite the worst quarterly correction in thirteen years in Q2. For junior gold investors, the FOMC on July 29 is not merely a rate announcement — it is the resolution event for the paradox that has kept gold range-bound between $3,950 and $4,130 for six weeks, and the catalyst that determines whether the autumn gold equity seasonal rally (historically averaging 10.1% for GDX) begins from $4,000 or $4,200.

headline: LI-FT POWER COMMENCES 163-HOLE, 38,970m LITHIUM DRILL AT ADINA-GALINÉE, QUÉBEC — One of the Largest Quebec Lithium Programs of 2026 (TSXV: LIFT)
snippet: Li-FT Power Ltd. (TSXV: LIFT) announced on July 17, 2026 that drilling has commenced at the Adina-Galinée Lithium Project in Quebec — a 163-hole, 38,970-metre program representing one of the largest hard-rock lithium drill campaigns in the province in 2026. The program combines 50-metre infill drilling to upgrade inferred resources and step-out expansion drilling on a large spodumene pegmatite complex assembled through the Winsome Resources acquisition and partnership agreements with Azimut Exploration and SOQUEM. Quebec's role as a preferred jurisdiction for battery-critical minerals — given its low-carbon hydroelectric power grid and proximity to North American battery manufacturing buildout — makes the Adina-Galinée scale relevant beyond the deposit parameters alone: large spodumene systems in Québec are the supply chain answer to US and EU battery manufacturing that does not depend on Australian or South American feedstock. For lithium equity investors, Li-FT's program size signals that management and project financiers are betting that the spodumene floor established at CNY 151,000 (approximately marginal cost for Australian operations) is durable enough to justify one of the largest systematic drill investments in Canadian hard-rock lithium currently underway.

headline: ALL 18 TRACKED RARE EARTH ELEMENTS ROSE IN JULY — Germanium +27.8%, Dysprosium +25.4%; NdPr at 2026 Highs; Defence Stockpile Procurement Absorbing Heavy Rare Earths
snippet: The July 2026 rare earth market data shows an unprecedented broad-based advance: all 18 tracked rare earth elements posted price gains simultaneously for the first time in 2026, led by germanium (+27.8%) and dysprosium (+25.4%), with NdPr alloy, neodymium, and praseodymium reaching new 2026 highs. The common driver across all 18 elements is defence and strategic stockpile procurement that accelerated following the IEA's July 16 stockpile recommendation and G7 procurement coordination signals — military-grade rare earth buyers (permanent magnets for missile guidance, EW systems, submarine motors) are absorbing heavy rare earths at a pace that does not respond to price in the way commercial buyers do. The AI/wind turbine demand component is providing additional floor support for NdPr: each next-generation wind turbine requires approximately 650 kg of NdPr, and each AI data centre GPU cluster uses rare-earth-containing power electronics and cooling systems. For North American rare earth equity investors, a month in which all 18 elements advance simultaneously is a signal that the China export restriction thesis has moved beyond selective tightening into broad supply constraint — the market structure that historically precedes the largest re-rating periods for jurisdictionally diversified rare earth developers.

headline: BMI RAISES 2026 COPPER FORECAST 6.7% TO $12,700/T — Sulphuric Acid Squeeze Modelled Explicitly; Structural Deficit Widens to 1.5M Tonnes by 2035
snippet: BMI (Fitch Solutions' commodity research division) raised its 2026 copper price forecast by 6.7% to $12,700 per tonne in a mid-July 2026 note — still below Macquarie's $13,165 and the Bloomberg consensus of $13,007, but notable for explicitly modelling the sulphuric acid supply squeeze as a named input to its revised forecast rather than treating it as a tail risk. BMI simultaneously cut its global mine production growth estimate to 2.4% for 2026, citing grade depletion at major Chilean operations and SX-EW curtailment risk from the acid disruption. The long-term structural deficit projection is the most significant element: BMI now models the copper supply gap widening from approximately 66,000 tonnes in 2027 to nearly 1.5 million tonnes per year by 2035 — driven by AI data centre power infrastructure, grid buildout for energy transition, and EV manufacturing — against a backdrop where no major new copper mine has reached production decision in the past 18 months. For junior copper exploration and development investors, BMI's 1.5-million-tonne deficit projection by 2035 provides the long-range demand framework that justifies exploration premium valuations for high-quality copper discoveries in stable jurisdictions, even at current capital costs.
